Each color is stored as a PaletteColor with a unique ID (int). You can apply a ColorScheme or a list of PaletteColor to this ColorPalette, which sets every PaletteColor contained in this palette to a matching PaletteColor in the scheme or list. Remarks The constructor: Clamps the configured minimum and maximum FPS to the static bounds (MinFpsLimit and MaxFpsLimit). Swaps min/max when they are supplied in the wrong order. api/ShapeEngine.Core.CollisionSystem.htm.summary: Namespace ShapeEngine.Core.CollisionSystem Classes CastSpaceEntry Represents a collection of colliders associated with a specific collision object, used for cast space queries. CastSpaceResult Represents the result of a cast space query, mapping collision objects to their associated colliders. CircleCollider Represents a circle collider for collision detection. CircleSectorCollider Represents a circle sector collider for collision detection. Collider Abstract base class for all colliders in the collision system. Collision Contains the information of an intersection or an overlap between two colliders. CollisionHandler Handles collision detection, resolution, and spatial queries for registered CollisionObject instances. Implements IBounds to provide bounding information for the collision system. CollisionInformation Contains the information of a collision between two collision objects in the form of a list of collisions. Each collision is an intersection or overlap between two colliders. CollisionObject Represents an object that participates in the collision system and can contain multiple colliders. Handles collision detection, intersection, and overlap logic, and provides events and hooks for collision notifications. CollisionPoints Represents a list of CollisionPoints, providing validation, filtering, and sorting utilities for collision detection. IntersectSpaceEntry Represents an entry in the intersection space, containing collision points and information about the other collider involved in the intersection. IntersectSpaceRegister Represents a register of intersection entries for a specific CollisionObject. IntersectSpaceResult Represents the result of an intersection space query, containing registers of intersection entries for multiple collision objects. LineCollider Represents an infinite line collider for collision detection. Overlap Represents an overlap between two colliders. PolyCollider Represents a polygon collider for collision detection, using a set of relative points. PolyLineCollider Represents a polyline collider for collision detection, using a set of relative points. QuadCollider Represents a quadrilateral (quad) collider for collision detection. RayCollider Represents a ray collider for collision detection. RectCollider Represents a rectangle collider for collision detection. SegmentCollider Represents a segment collider for collision detection. SpatialHash Implements a spatial hash grid for efficient broad-phase collision detection and spatial queries. SpatialHash.Bucket Represents a collection of colliders within a single spatial hash bucket. TriangleCollider Represents a triangle collider for collision detection. Interfaces IShape Interface for all shape types used in the collision system. Enums CollisionPointsFilterType Specifies the method used to filter or select collision points from a set of detected collisions. ShapeType Represents the different types of shapes supported by the collision system.

Used for DrawGappedOutline functions. public readonly struct GappedOutlineDrawingInfo Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Constructors GappedOutlineDrawingInfo(int, float, float) Initializes a new instance of the GappedOutlineDrawingInfo struct. public GappedOutlineDrawingInfo(int gaps, float startOffset = 0, float gapPerimeterPercentage = 0.5) Parameters gaps int The count of outline areas that are not drawn. The count of outline areas drawn always equals the count of gaps. startOffset float Value between 0 and 1 to change where the first part is drawn (useful for animating it). The offset value is wrapped between 0 and 1. Examples: 1.5 would result in 0.5. -0.2 would result in 0.8 gapPerimeterPercentage float How much of the total perimeter should be a gap (not drawn). 1 - gapPercentage equals the total amount of perimeter drawn. If 0 normal outline is drawn, if 1 nothing is drawn. Fields GapPerimeterPercentage The fraction of the total perimeter that should be a gap (not drawn). public readonly float GapPerimeterPercentage Field Value float Remarks The total drawn perimeter is divided equally among all drawn segments. Gaps The number of gap segments (not drawn) in the outline. The number of drawn segments always equals the number of gaps. public readonly int Gaps Field Value int Examples For example: 6 gaps result in 6 drawn segments and 6 gaps. If GapPerimeterPercentage is 0.5, all segments and gaps are equal in length. If GapPerimeterPercentage is 0.75, then 75% of the perimeter is divided into 6 gaps and 25% into 6 drawn segments. Remarks The total gap length, defined by GapPerimeterPercentage, is divided equally among all Gaps. The total drawn length, defined by 1 - GapPerimeterPercentage, is also divided equally among all Gaps. StartOffset Value between 0 and 1 to change where the first part is drawn (useful for animating it). The offset value is wrapped between 0 and 1. public readonly float StartOffset Field Value float Examples For example: If startOffset is 1.5, it wraps to 0.5. If startOffset is -0.2, it wraps to 0.8. api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.C.summary: Class CellCollisionSystem Namespace ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Cell-based collision system that partitions world space into a grid of cells of the specified size. Manages registration of ICellCollider instances, updates their positions each frame, moves them between cells, and invokes enter/exit and collision start/end callbacks accordingly. public class CellCollisionSystem Inheritance object CellCollisionSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Constructors CellCollisionSystem(Size) Cell-based collision system that partitions world space into a grid of cells of the specified size. Manages registration of ICellCollider instances, updates their positions each frame, moves them between cells, and invokes enter/exit and collision start/end callbacks accordingly. public CellCollisionSystem(Size cellSize) Parameters cellSize Size Size of each grid cell in world units (width and height). Methods Add(ICellCollider) Request registration of a collider with the cell collision system. If the collider is currently scheduled for removal this frame, the add will be rejected. The collider is enqueued and will be processed by ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.CellCollisionSystem.ProcessPendingColliders() on the next update. public bool Add(ICellCollider collider) Parameters collider ICellCollider The ICellCollider to add. Returns bool True if the collider was successfully queued for addition; false if it was already scheduled for removal or already present in the add queue. Clear() Clears the collision system state and returns all pooled resources. public void Clear() Remarks This method clears the pending add/remove queues, unregisters all colliders, and returns any allocated pooled CellCollisionSystem.Cell instances back to the pool. After calling Clear(), the system will be in an empty state with no registered colliders or active cells. Close() Closes the collision system and releases any managed resources. public void Close() Remarks This currently delegates to Clear() to unregister colliders and return pooled cell instances. DrawDebug(ColorRgba, ColorRgba, ColorRgba) Draws a debug visualization of the collision grid. Renders grid lines for all tracked cells, optionally fills occupied cells, and draws an outer bounding rectangle around the active cell area. public void DrawDebug(ColorRgba lineColor, ColorRgba fillColor, ColorRgba borderColor) Parameters lineColor ColorRgba Color used to draw the grid lines for each cell. fillColor ColorRgba Color used to fill cells that contain occupants. borderColor ColorRgba Color used to draw the bounding rectangle around all active cells. GetAllColliders<T>(ref HashSet<T>) Copies all registered colliders of type T into the provided result set. Iterates the internal registry and adds any collider that can be cast to T. public int GetAllColliders<T>(ref HashSet<T> result) where T : ICellCollider Parameters result HashSet<T> A reference to a HashSet<T> that will be populated with matching colliders. The set is modified in-place; duplicates are ignored. Returns int The number of colliders added to result by this call. Type Parameters T The collider concrete type to filter for. Must implement ICellCollider. Remove(ICellCollider) Schedule a collider to be unregistered from the collision system. If the collider is currently queued for addition this frame, it will be removed from the add queue. The actual removal will be processed by ShapeEngine.Geometry.CellCollision.CellCollisionSystem.ProcessPendingColliders() on the next update, which will call RemoveCollider(ICellCollider) to perform the removal and trigger any necessary exit/collision end callbacks. public bool Remove(ICellCollider collider) Parameters collider ICellCollider The ICellCollider instance to remove. Returns bool True if the collider was successfully queued for removal (i.e. added to the internal removal set); false if it was already present in the removal queue. Update(float) Advance the collision system by a single frame. This will process any pending additions/removals, update all registered colliders' positions by dt, and resolve collisions for colliders that moved between cells during this update. public void Update(float dt) Parameters dt float Delta time in seconds since the last update.

OnCollisionStartedWith(ICellCollider) Called when a collision with other has started. Constructors BroadphaseSpatialHash(Rect, Size) Initializes a new instance of the BroadphaseSpatialHash class using the provided bounding rectangle and a desired bucket size. Remarks The values of SpacingX and SpacingY are derived from the resolved Rows and Cols (rather than being set directly from bucketSize). api/ShapeEngine.Geometry.CollisionSystem.summary: Enum BroadphaseType Namespace ShapeEngine.Geometry.CollisionSystem Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Specifies the broadphase collision detection strategy for a collider. FullShape is the default. public enum BroadphaseType Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Fields BoundingBox = 1 Balanced performance for general use cases. The bounding box is used for broadphase checks, but not the full shape. This is not recommended for very large objects. Especially large thin objects, like lines, segments, or rays. FullShape = 2 Suited for large or complicated objects where precise querying is needed. Only a point is used for broadphase checks.

BroadphaseColliderRegister<T> Manages a register of colliders and their associated data for broadphase collision detection. BroadphaseDynamicSpatialHash Implements a dynamic spatial hash broadphase for collision detection. Efficiently manages colliders in spatial buckets for fast broadphase queries. Only creates and stores buckets that contain colliders, optimizing memory usage. Old buckets that become empty are recycled for future use. Does not maintain persistent bounds; bounds are recalculated each frame based on added colliders. BroadphaseSpatialHash Implements a spatial hash grid for efficient broad-phase collision detection and spatial queries. CastSpaceResult Represents the result of a cast space query, mapping collision objects to their associated colliders. Collider Abstract base class for all colliders in the collision system. Collision Contains the information of an intersection or an overlap between two colliders. CollisionInformation Contains the information of a collision between two collision objects in the form of a list of collisions. Each collision is an intersection or overlap between two colliders. CollisionObject Represents an object that participates in the collision system and can contain multiple colliders. Handles collision detection, intersection, and overlap logic, and provides events and hooks for collision notifications. IntersectSpaceEntry Represents an entry in the intersection space, containing collision points and information about the other collider involved in the intersection. IntersectionPoints Represents a list of IntersectionPoints, providing validation, filtering, and sorting utilities for collision detection. Overlap Represents an overlap between two colliders. CollisionPointValidationResult Represents the result of validating collision points, containing various relevant points. IntersectionPoint Represents a single intersection point, including its position and normal vector. Interfaces IBroadphase Represents a broadphase collision detection system interface. LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Remarks Points should be provided in CCW order for correct geometric calculations. Use FixWindingOrder() or MakeCounterClockwise() if your points are in clockwise (CW) order. A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. In other words, no vertices "point inward." A concave polygon is a polygon that has at least one interior angle greater than 180°, and at least one line segment between points inside the polygon passes outside the polygon. This means it has at least one "caved-in" or inward-pointing vertex. IsClockwise() Determines if the polygon's winding order is clockwise. public bool IsClockwise() Returns bool True if clockwise; otherwise, false. IsConvex() Determines if the polygon is convex. public bool IsConvex() Returns bool True if convex; otherwise, false. Remarks A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. In other words, no vertices "point inward." A concave polygon is a polygon that has at least one interior angle greater than 180°, and at least one line segment between points inside the polygon passes outside the polygon. This means it has at least one "caved-in" or inward-pointing vertex. Returns bool True if the polygon is convex; otherwise, false. Remarks Convex: A convex polygon is a polygon where all interior angles are less than 180°, and every line segment between any two points inside the polygon lies entirely within the polygon. This means none of its vertices "point inward," and the polygon does not have any indentations. Concave: A concave polygon has at least one interior angle greater than 180° and at least one vertex that points inward (self-intersecting). Provides methods for geometric operations and shape conversions. PolylineCollider Represents a polyline collider for collision detection, using a set of relative points. TriangleShape Represents a triangle shape that can be transformed and recalculated based on three relative points. Structs Triangle Represents a triangle defined by three vertices in 2D space. The vertices should be arranged in counter-clockwise order for proper geometric calculations.

api/ShapeEngine.Input.ModifierKeySet.htm.summary: Class ModifierKeySet Namespace ShapeEngine.Input Assembly ShapeEngine.dll A set of modifier keys that are evaluated together based on a specified operator. public class ModifierKeySet : IEquatable<ModifierKeySet>, ICopyable<ModifierKeySet> Inheritance object ModifierKeySet Implements IEquatable<ModifierKeySet> ICopyable<ModifierKeySet> Inherited Members object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Examples Any combination of modifier keys is allowed. However, gamepad-related modifier keys only function with gamepad-related input. For example, while "[Shift] + Right Bumper" is technically valid, the order and context matter: "[Right Bumper] + Shift" does not work because gamepad modifiers require a gamepad input context. Combinations like "[Shift] + Left Mouse Button" or "[Middle Mouse Button] + Space" are valid, as they involve keyboard or mouse modifiers. Always ensure that gamepad modifiers are paired with gamepad inputs for correct behavior. So you can pair any modifier type with gamepad input, but gamepad modifiers will only work with gamepad input. Remarks This class is used to define combinations of modifier keys (like Shift, Ctrl, Alt) that must be active for an input to be triggered. The keys can be combined using either an AND or an OR logic. api/ShapeEngine.Input.html.title: Namespace ShapeEngine.Input | ShapeEngine
api/ShapeEngine.Input.html.summary: Namespace ShapeEngine.Input Classes GamepadDevice Represents a gamepad input device, providing access to gamepad buttons and axes, state tracking, calibration, and utility methods for gamepad input. GamepadDeviceManager Manages multiple GamepadDevice instances, handling connection state, device claiming, releasing, and tracking last used gamepads. InputAction Represents an input action, which can be triggered by various input types and devices. Handles state, multi-tap, hold, and axis sensitivity/gravity. InputActionTree Represents a sorted collection of InputAction objects, ordered by their execution order and ID. Provides methods for updating and retrieving input actions based on various criteria. Implements a blocking system for IInputTypes. When an InputAction in this tree is processed and its BlocksInput property is set to true, it blocks the associated IInputTypes from being used by subsequent InputActions in the same update cycle. This ensures that input types are only handled by the first eligible action, preventing conflicts or duplicate processing. InputActionTreeGroup Represents a sorted collection of InputActionTree objects. Provides methods for updating and retrieving input action trees based on various criteria. InputDevice Represents a generic input device interface for the ShapeEngine input system. Provides methods for device usage tracking, locking, and calibration. InputEvent Represents an input event from a keyboard, mouse, or gamepad device. InputExtensions Provides extension methods for input-related types, such as device type filtering, input state retrieval, consumption, creation, and display name formatting. InputGesture Represents a gesture logic for an InputAction. Handles tap, multi-tap, long press, and long release gestures, tracking progress, state, and completion. InputSettings Represents the settings for detecting input device usage, including mouse, keyboard, and gamepad. InputSettings.GamepadSettings Represents the settings used for detecting gamepad input device usage, including thresholds and detection options. InputSettings.KeyboardSettings Represents the settings used for detecting keyboard input device usage, including thresholds and detection options. InputSettings.MouseSettings Represents the settings used for detecting mouse input device usage, including thresholds and detection options. InputSystem Represents the main input system for managing input devices, input actions, and access control. Handles device updates, action trees, and provides locking mechanisms for input processing. InputTypeGamepadButton Represents an input type for a gamepad button, supporting deadzone and modifier keys. InputTypeGamepadButtonAxis Represents an input type for a gamepad button axis (negative and positive buttons), supporting deadzone and modifier keys. InputTypeGamepadJoyAxis Represents an input type for a gamepad joystick axis, supporting deadzone and modifier keys. InputTypeGamepadTriggerAxis Represents an input type for a gamepad trigger axis, supporting deadzone and modifier keys. InputTypeKeyboardButton Represents an input type for a keyboard button, supporting modifier keys. InputTypeKeyboardButtonAxis Represents an input type for a keyboard button axis (negative and positive buttons), supporting modifier keys. InputTypeMouseAxis Represents an input type for a mouse axis, supporting deadzone and modifier keys. InputTypeMouseButton Represents an input type for a mouse button, supporting deadzone and modifier keys. InputTypeMouseButtonAxis Represents an input type for a mouse button axis (negative and positive buttons), supporting deadzone and modifier keys. InputTypeMousePositionDelta Represents an input type that tracks the delta of the mouse position relative to a target position. Supports deadzone threshold and optional modifier keys. InputTypeMouseWheelAxis Represents an input type for a mouse wheel axis, supporting deadzone and modifier keys. KeyboardDevice Represents a keyboard input device, providing access to keyboard buttons, state tracking, character input, and utility methods for keyboard input. ModifierKeyGamepadButton Represents a modifier key that is mapped to a gamepad button. ModifierKeyKeyboardButton Represents a modifier key that is mapped to a keyboard button. ModifierKeyMouseButton Represents a modifier key that is mapped to a mouse button. ModifierKeySet A set of modifier keys that are evaluated together based on a specified operator. MouseDevice Represents a mouse input device, providing access to mouse buttons, axes, and wheel axes, as well as state tracking and utility methods for mouse input. Structs InputActionSettings Represents settings for input actions, including axis sensitivity and gravity. Implements IEquatable<T> for value equality. InputGesture.Result Represents the result of an InputGesture update. Contains the gesture type, current state, and normalized progress. InputName Represents a named input associated with a specific input device type. InputState Represents the state of an input, including button presses, axis values, device type, and input gesture details. Interfaces IInputType Represents an input type abstraction for various input devices (keyboard, mouse, gamepad). Provides methods for copying, deadzone management, state retrieval, and device identification. IModifierKey Represents a modifier key (such as Shift, Ctrl, Alt) for input handling. Enums InputAction.ToggleState Represents the toggle state for an input action. InputDeviceType Represents the type of input device. InputGesture.State Represents the possible states of an InputGesture. InputGesture.Type Represents the types of gesture for an InputGesture. ModifierKeyOperator Specifies the logical operator to use when evaluating modifier keys. ShapeGamepadButton Represents the various buttons available on a gamepad. ShapeGamepadJoyAxis Represents the joystick axes (left and right sticks) of a gamepad. ShapeGamepadTriggerAxis Represents the trigger axes (left and right triggers) of a gamepad. ShapeKeyboardButton Represents keyboard buttons for the ShapeEngine input system. The enum values correspond to their respective key codes. ShapeMouseAxis Represents the axes of mouse movement. ShapeMouseButton Represents mouse buttons and mouse wheel/axis actions for input handling. ShapeMouseWheelAxis Specifies the axis of the mouse wheel movement.

api/ShapeEngine.Pathfinding.html.title: Namespace ShapeEngine.Pathfinding | ShapeEngine
api/ShapeEngine.Pathfinding.html.summary: Namespace ShapeEngine.Pathfinding Classes Path Represents a path used by the pathfinding system. Contains the start and end positions and the sequence of rectangles that form the path. Instances are intended to be rented from and returned to an internal pool using RentPath(Vector2, Vector2, int) and ReturnPath(Path) to minimize allocations. PathRequest Represents a request for a path from an agent, including start/end positions and priority. Pathfinder A grid based pathfinder that uses A* to find paths for agents. Structs NodeCost Represents a cost that can be applied to a node, affecting its traversability or weight. Interfaces IPathfinderAgent Interface for agents that can request and receive paths from a Pathfinder. IPathfinderObstacle Represents an obstacle in the pathfinding system. Inherits from IShape. Enums NodeCostType Enumerates the types of node value operations that can be applied to a node.

api/ShapeEngine.Random.ChanceList-1.html.summary: Class ChanceList<T> Namespace ShapeEngine.Random Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Represents a list of values with weighted chances for random selection. public class ChanceList<T> Type Parameters T The type of values in the list. Inheritance object ChanceList<T> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Remarks The list is populated with each value repeated according to its specified amount, representing its weight in the selection process. Each time a random value is picked, it is removed from the list, ensuring that every value is selected exactly as many times as its weight before the list is refilled with the original entries. This guarantees proportional selection: for example, if value A appears 10 times and value B appears 5 times, then over 15 picks, value A will always be chosen 10 times and value B 5 times, in a randomized order. api/ShapeEngine.Screen.ScreenTextureMode.summary: Enum ScreenTextureMode Namespace ShapeEngine.Screen Assembly ShapeEngine.dll Specifies the different modes for handling screen textures. public enum ScreenTextureMode Extension Methods ShapeLogger.Log(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogConsole(object, string, LogLevel) ShapeLogger.LogFile(object, string, LogLevel) Fields Anchor = 16 Texture size will be calculated as screensize multiplied by anchorstretch, and the top-left position will be screensize multiplied by anchorposition. Custom = 32 Custom mode for user-defined texture sizing and positioning logic. Fixed = 4 Texture will always be the same size and centered on the screen. NearestFixed = 8 Texture will always maintain the same aspect ratio as the screen but will stay as close as possible to the fixed dimensions. If zero or negative, the method calculates it automatically. Providing a known length avoids redundant calculations and improves performance, especially for static segments. lineInfo LineDrawingInfo Parameters describing how to draw the segment. gapDrawingInfo GappedOutlineDrawingInfo Parameters describing the gap configuration. Produces smooth, continuous noise values (approximately in the range [-1, 1]) for given world coordinates scaled by a lattice cell size (gridSize). Maintains a static cache of pseudo-random gradient vectors and exposes an integer Seed to change the generated gradients. Changing Seed clears the gradient cache. Note: the internal gradient cache is not synchronized; use external synchronization for concurrent access. public static class PerlinNoise2D Inheritance object PerlinNoise2D Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties Seed Gets or sets the integer seed used to generate pseudo-random gradient vectors. Setting a new value clears the cached gradient table so subsequent noise samples use gradients derived from the new seed. public static int Seed { get; set; } Property Value int The seed value. Default is 0. Methods Noise(float, float, float) Generates a 2D Perlin Noise value for a given coordinate (x, y) at a specified grid scale. The noise is smooth, continuous, and typically normalized to the range [-1.0, 1.0]. public static float Noise(float x, float y, float gridSize) Parameters x float The world/sample X coordinate. Interpreted in the same units as gridSize. y float The world/sample Y coordinate. Interpreted in the same units as gridSize. gridSize float The size of each lattice cell. Larger values produce lower-frequency (smoother) noise; smaller values produce higher-frequency detail. Returns float Perlin noise value at (x,y), approximately in the range [-1, 1].

index.html.summary: My custom-made engine based on the great Raylib Framework. The Main focus is being performant and only using draw functions instead of textures. When using Shape Engine everything from Raylib is available as well. (Raylib Examples, Raylib Cheatsheet) Shape Engine´s examples are available on Itch as well and it is a great way to support me :) More examples are available in the ShapeEngineDemos repository. Most of the bigger examples will be available here, like a small asteroids game. You are free to use Shape Engine or any part of Shape Engine for your own projects, but keep in mind that Shape Engine was designed to help me with my specific game dev needs. Nevertheless I am looking forward to creations that Shape Engine made possible :) Release Trailer Showcase Installation / How to Use There are multiple ways to use Shape Engine: Create a new solution & project and download Shape Engine from the Nuget manager. (Recommended) dotnet new console -n ShapeEngineProject cd ./ShapeEngineProject dotnet add package DaveGreen.ShapeEngine Clone or fork the repository and add new projects to the solution. You then can reference the Shape Engine project and start working on your game. The advantages are that you can easily change things in Shape Engine and everything updates automatically in your own project. Create a new solution & project in a .net IDE. (Visual Studio / JetBrains Rider for example). Download or fork ShapeEngine and either create a local nuget package or build the solution to create all necessary dll files. [Using a local Nuget Package] Create a folder on your machine called something like “Local Nuget Packages” and copy the ShapeEngine Nuget package that you created to this folder. (You can also add the Shape Engine Nuget package directly to your Project). Now you need to create a new Package source in the Nuget Manager that points to your “Local Nuget Packages” Folder. This source can be used in your Nuget Manager to find and install the Shape Engine Nuget Package. You manually copy all needed DLL files to your project. You need the following DLLs: Clipper2Lib, Raylib-Cs, Microsoft.Toolkit.HighPerformance, Shape Engine Core, Raylib. All DLL files except Raylib can be anywhere in your projects folder hierarchy. The Raylib DLL must be on the root level of your project. You need to select the right Raylib DLL for your operating system. Now just add a reference for all DLLs except the Raylib DLL and you are done. On MacOS you need to do the same step except using the .dylib file instead of the raylib DLL. You need to set the property “Copy if Newer” to true on the .dylib file. Then everything should work. Create a new solution & project and just add the Shape Engine Core DLL to your project and reference it. Now you need to download the right version of the Raylib_CsLo & Clipper2 Nuget packages. The releases on GitHub will state which versions were used. Minimal Project Setup // Program.cs using System.Drawing; using ShapeEngine.Color; using ShapeEngine.Core; using ShapeEngine.Core.Structs; using ShapeEngine.StaticLib.Drawing; namespace ShapeEngineProject; public static class Program { public static void Main(string[] args) { var game = new MyGameClass(GameSettings.StretchMode, WindowSettings.Default); game.Run(); } } public class MyGameClass : Game { public MyGameClass(GameSettings gameSettings, WindowSettings windowSettings) : base(gameSettings, windowSettings) { } protected override void DrawGame(ScreenInfo game) { game.Area.Draw(new ColorRgba(Color.DarkOliveGreen)); game.Area.DrawLines(12f, new ColorRgba(Color.AntiqueWhite)); game.MousePos.Draw(24f, new ColorRgba(Color.Lime), 36); } } Development Process The Main Branch contains the current development stage. You can follow the development process here: Reddit Twitter Instagram YouTube GitHub Discussions Roadmap Examples You can download the newest builds of the Example Project on Itch io. You can clone the repo and inspect the example projects there as well. Examples are simple scenes that focus on one specific area or feature of Shape Engine. Examples showcase the various capabilities of Shape Engine, allowing users to explore various features. The examples cover all major features of Shape Engine, ensuring that users can grasp its full potential. Features In general my goal is to provide the most relevant system a game dev needs without adding a solution for every possible problem. Polygon Fracturing Delaunay Triangulation Text & Font System Word Emphasis System Pathfinding UI System Collision System Audio & Music Savegame System Color Palettes Input System (Keyboard, Mouse, Gamepad) Camera System Screen Texture System Gapped Drawing Striped Drawing Shape Collision System 2.0 with Segment, Line, Ray, Circle, Triangle, Quad, Rect, Polygon, Polyline Dependencies I am just using the Raylib Cs c# bindings and the Cipper2 library for polygon clipping. If you use the nuget manager to download Shape Engine as a nuget package you don't have to take care of any dependencies, because they will be downloaded automatically. Limitations There is no physics system because I don´t need one and would´t know how to make one. There is complete collision system but the collision response is up to you. You can also use raylibs physics system. History I made Shape Engine because I wanted to help myself make games with a specific art style and certain limitations. At first, it started out with some helper scripts but now it is a relatively sophisticated system to make games with raylib. Certain parts of the basic game loop are inspired by Bytepath and other things I already used in games that I made myself (especially Fracture Hell). Feel free to use any single part if you don´t want to use the whole package. Contact If you have an issue, or a suggestion for a new feature GitHub is the best way to get in contact with me. GitHub Issues GitHub Discussions On these platforms you can follow the development process of Shape Engine, get in contact with me and always stay up date.
